item.title: Implement rate limiter per SPEC.md in ratelimit.py
item.brief: Implement the rate limiter described in SPEC.md in ratelimit.py. The module currently only has stubs. Follow the spec exactly, including its error cases and edge cases. The tests in test_ratelimit.py only cover the basics, so verify the error cases and edge cases in SPEC.md beyond what those tests check. Keep the implementation dependency-free (Python standard library only). Commit the work on the local branch; do not push. Do not change SPEC.md or the existing tests to make them pass.

pr.body:
Approach: TokenBucket keeps tokens and the latest clock time seen; refill only moves forward when the clock advances, so a backwards clock changes nothing. KeyedLimiter keeps an OrderedDict of buckets, moves a key to the end on each use (try_acquire and wait_time), and evicts the least recently used key before creating a new one. Invalid request sizes are rejected before any bucket is created or evicted.

Key files: ratelimit.py, test_ratelimit_spec.py (new). test_ratelimit.py and SPEC.md unchanged.

Checks: unittest 22 OK; ruff check and ruff format --check clean. Mutant check: with the tolerance set to 0, the large-capacity test fails 9 of 300 cases.

Assumptions and limits: (1) A relative tolerance of 1e-12 * capacity absorbs float rounding so the wait_time promise holds. This lets a deficit below that amount succeed, a small deviation from the literal SPEC. (2) Not thread-safe; no locking was specified. (3) Clock resolution limits the promise for very large monotonic clock values.
pr.summary: Made rate limiting available: TokenBucket and KeyedLimiter per SPEC.md. Now: refill capped at capacity, non-consuming wait_time, LRU eviction bounded by max_keys, ValueError on invalid args. Before: module was stubs raising NotImplementedError; now: 22 tests pass.
